Chapter 7: The Meaning of Existence and the Purpose of Life.
You ever find yourself wondering, late at night or in a quiet moment, why you’re really here? It’s a question that’s been with us for as long as people have shared stories. What’s the point of all this—this mix of joy, pain, beginnings, endings? Is there a deeper purpose hiding behind everything we experience?
Picture a young artist, struggling to find her voice in a world that never seems to stop shouting. She’s surrounded by the endless noise of social media and the pressure to stand out. There are days when she feels tiny—like nothing she does could possibly matter. But one evening, after a long battle with self-doubt, she sits down in front of a blank canvas. Instead of overthinking, she just lets her feelings pour out—color, shape, movement. And in that moment, as she creates, something shifts. She feels a quiet connection—a sense that what she’s doing is enough. That meaning isn’t about the finished painting or how many likes it gets. It’s about the simple act of creating.
In the conversation with God, there’s this idea that the purpose of life isn’t some big achievement waiting for us at the finish line. It’s something we get to experience every single day. Most of us are taught to hunt for meaning in our accomplishments, our relationships, or the recognition we get from others. Happiness always feels just out of reach—one more goal away. But what if meaning is already here, woven into every breath, every act of kindness, every moment we choose courage over fear?
Imagine an older man, looking back on his life. He’s had his share of ups and downs, and now he wonders: Did I really make a difference? He starts to remember the little things—a smile he shared with a stranger, a few kind words to a friend, a quiet moment of generosity when no one was watching. Suddenly, it hits him. The purpose of life isn’t measured by big achievements. It’s about showing up fully in each moment. Meaning isn’t something we stumble across—it’s something we create, with every choice we make.
Most of us don’t even realize how much we chase after meaning, thinking it’s some prize waiting for us out there. But what if it’s actually made right here, by the way we choose to live? It’s in showing up, in loving deeply, in risking vulnerability, and in embracing the sheer mystery of being alive.
Maybe the purpose of life isn’t about dodging pain or chasing after pleasure. Maybe it’s about growing in awareness. Opening our hearts wider. Remembering who we really are. Each one of us is a unique expression of something greater—a single note in the symphony of existence. The invitation? Play your note as fully as you can. Bring your true self to the dance. And trust that your life matters, simply because you’re here.
